mechanisms.name: Autosave and offline drafts
mechanisms.why: Edits persist continuously and survive crashes and flaky connections.

mechanisms.name: Drag and drop import of media
mechanisms.why: Dropping images, video or files onto the canvas is the fastest way to start a project.

mechanisms.name: In browser video export
mechanisms.why: Encoding timelines on device with WebCodecs avoids server queues and uploads.

mechanisms.name: GPU accelerated canvas rendering
mechanisms.why: Pan and zoom of huge documents stays smooth; Figma renders with WebGPU and falls back to WebGL mid session.

mechanisms.name: Multiplayer cursors and presence
mechanisms.why: Seeing collaborators' pointers in real time makes shared canvases feel live; Canva uses WebRTC data channels with a WebSocket fallback.

mechanisms.name: Pen pressure, tilt and coalesced input
mechanisms.why: Natural strokes need pressure, tilt and every intermediate point, not just frame rate samples.

mechanisms.name: Real-time document sync (last writer wins registers)
mechanisms.why: Per property last writer wins ordered by a central server gives simple, conflict free multiplayer without full CRDT cost.

mechanisms.name: Edit audio and video by editing text
mechanisms.why: Deleting words in a transcript cuts the media, making editing as easy as a document.

mechanisms.name: Undo, redo and version history
mechanisms.why: Fearless experimentation depends on multi step undo and named restore points, which collaboration complicates.

mechanisms.name: WebAssembly engine core
mechanisms.why: C++ editor cores compiled with Emscripten give near native speed and share code with server rendering.

mechanisms.name: AI generation and enhancement panels
mechanisms.why: Prompt panels for images, copy, voice cleanup and background removal sit next to the canvas.

mechanisms.name: Auto generated editable captions
mechanisms.why: Speech to text creates timed caption blocks users can retime and style.

mechanisms.name: Templates, brand kit and one click resize
mechanisms.why: Brand colors, fonts and logos auto apply, and one design resizes to many channel formats.

mechanisms.name: Open and save real files from disk
mechanisms.why: Direct file handles let web editors behave like desktop apps with save in place.

mechanisms.name: Installed font access
mechanisms.why: Designers expect their installed fonts in the picker; this needs a permission prompt and is Chromium only.

mechanisms.name: Rich clipboard copy and paste
mechanisms.why: Pasting images, SVG and styled text between apps keeps design work flowing.

mechanisms.name: Device capability and network detection
mechanisms.why: Pick codec, bitrate and quality by whether playback is smooth and power efficient; Network Information is limited availability so degrade gracefully.

mechanisms.name: Passkey sign in
mechanisms.why: WebAuthn replaces passwords and SMS codes; Baseline since 2021 and cuts friction for returning users.

mechanisms.name: Payments and subscriptions
mechanisms.why: Browser managed checkout reduces forms for subscriptions and in app purchases; Digital Goods API is aimed at Play Billing in Android PWAs (not verified on MDN here).

mechanisms.name: Push notifications for new content
mechanisms.why: Re-engages viewers for new episodes, live starts and releases via a service worker push event. Baseline widely available.

mechanisms.name: Low latency sync with WebTransport and WebSocket
mechanisms.why: Live chat, multiplayer state and shared playback need low latency streams; WebTransport adds datagrams and multiple streams over HTTP/3 and is Baseline 2026.

mechanisms.name: Reduced motion and accessibility
mechanisms.why: Honor prefers-reduced-motion for autoplay, parallax and transitions to avoid vestibular triggers; pair with captions, sign language and screen reader support as the awards reward.

mechanisms.name: Storage persistence and quota
mechanisms.why: Request persistent storage so offline downloads and projects are not evicted, and read estimate() for quota planning. Baseline widely available.

mechanisms.name: Screen wake lock during play
mechanisms.why: Keeps the screen on for video, reading, recipes and streams; must be re-requested after visibilitychange and may be rejected on low battery.

mechanisms.name: App badging
mechanisms.why: Shows an unread or new content count on the app icon without a disruptive notification. Limited availability.

mechanisms.name: Background fetch for downloads
mechanisms.why: Hands large movie, audio and game downloads to the browser with progress UI so they survive navigation. Experimental, limited availability.

mechanisms.name: Compute Pressure adaptation
mechanisms.why: Observe CPU and thermal state (nominal to critical) to lower effects, encode quality or AI work before frames drop. Experimental.

mechanisms.name: WebGPU and WebGL rendering
mechanisms.why: High fidelity visuals and GPU compute for games and creative tools; WebGPU is limited availability so keep a WebGL fallback.

mechanisms.name: Haptics and vibration feedback
mechanisms.why: Tactile cues make rhythm, card opening and accessibility feedback feel physical; Apple awarded haptic heavy games. Safari lacks navigator.vibrate so feature detect.

mechanisms.name: Screen orientation lock
mechanisms.why: Lock to landscape for games and fullscreen video; typically requires fullscreen on mobile and has limited availability.

mechanisms.name: Install as PWA
mechanisms.why: Installed web apps get their own window and icon, bringing web media apps close to native feel. Needs a manifest and a user confirmed prompt.

mechanisms.name: View transitions between screens
mechanisms.why: Animated state changes between views in SPAs and MPAs give native feeling navigation for media browsing.

mechanisms.name: Speech recognition voice search
mechanisms.why: Voice queries and dictation via SpeechRecognition; recognition is often server side and support varies by browser.

mechanisms.name: Web Share and share targets
mechanisms.why: Native share sheet for clips, playlists and results; the separate Web Share Target API lets an installed PWA receive shares.

mechanisms.name: WebXR immersive sessions
mechanisms.why: Immersive video, spatial puzzles and 3D shopping on headsets, a category Google Play and Apple now award. Limited availability and experimental.

mechanisms.name: Cloud game streaming over WebRTC
mechanisms.why: Low latency and packet loss resilience decide whether a streamed game feels playable in a browser.

mechanisms.name: Deep links into a game or server
mechanisms.why: A shared link must open the app straight into a specific game, server or lobby with launch data.

mechanisms.name: Embedded multiplayer activities in an iframe
mechanisms.why: Web apps run inside Discord via an iframe and SDK so friends can play together in a voice channel.

mechanisms.name: Fullscreen immersive play
mechanisms.why: Fullscreen removes browser chrome so the game fills the display.

mechanisms.name: Gamepad input mapping and hot plug
mechanisms.why: Controller buttons and axes must map to game actions, with connect and disconnect handled live.

mechanisms.name: Keyboard lock in fullscreen
mechanisms.why: Games need Escape and browser shortcut keys delivered to the stream instead of the browser.

mechanisms.name: Pointer lock for mouse look
mechanisms.why: First person games need raw unbounded mouse deltas with the cursor hidden.

mechanisms.name: Live presence and chat over WebSocket
mechanisms.why: Persistent sockets deliver friend presence, voice state and in game chat in real time.

mechanisms.name: Keep screen awake during play
mechanisms.why: Long sessions and streams must not be interrupted by the screen dimming or locking.

mechanisms.name: Controller first spatial navigation
mechanisms.why: Directional focus movement makes store and library UIs usable from a gamepad or TV remote.

mechanisms.name: On screen touch controls for streamed games
mechanisms.why: Touch layouts let phone players play without a controller; Microsoft reports 20 percent use touch exclusively.

mechanisms.name: Achievement unlock toasts and progress
mechanisms.why: Visible unlock moments reward players and drive completion and sharing.

mechanisms.name: Supported browser and codec gating
mechanisms.why: Cloud gaming only runs on browsers with the required codecs and input APIs, so services gate by browser and version.

mechanisms.name: Clip and highlight recording
mechanisms.why: Recording a MediaStream lets players save and post a moment without leaving the game.

mechanisms.name: Always on top mini window overlay
mechanisms.why: A floating window keeps chat or voice controls visible while the player stays in another app.

mechanisms.name: Push notifications for friends and releases
mechanisms.why: Notifications bring players back for friend invites, sales and live streams.

mechanisms.name: Controller haptic feedback (rumble)
mechanisms.why: Rumble gives tactile feedback that streamed games rely on for impact and damage cues.

mechanisms.name: Embeddable HTML5 game frame with fullscreen button
mechanisms.why: Browser games embed in other pages and need an explicit fullscreen path from inside an iframe.

mechanisms.name: Media keys and lock screen controls
mechanisms.why: Hardware keys and lock screen controls keep streams and game audio controllable when the tab is hidden.

mechanisms.name: Remote Play with Steam Input configs
mechanisms.why: Remote Play streams a game to phones and TVs using Steam Input touch and controller layouts.

mechanisms.name: Screen and tab capture for sharing
mechanisms.why: Players share their screen or game window with friends or streams.

mechanisms.name: Hardware decode with per frame control
mechanisms.why: Direct codec access can cut decode and render delay in streamed video.

mechanisms.name: Unreliable datagrams for real time state
mechanisms.why: Datagrams give low latency, loss tolerant transport for input and game state.

mechanisms.name: Real time channel events via EventSub
mechanisms.why: Chat, follows and subscriptions arrive as pushed events over WebSocket or webhook.

mechanisms.name: Adaptive bitrate tuned for low latency
mechanisms.why: Standard ABR rebuffers at low latency, so players need algorithms built for small buffers.

mechanisms.name: Low latency HLS delivery
mechanisms.why: Partial segments and blocking playlist reloads cut glass to glass delay to a few seconds.

mechanisms.name: Adaptive playback through Media Source
mechanisms.why: Script fed buffers let players switch renditions and manage latency for live video.

mechanisms.name: Server streamed live chat
mechanisms.why: A streaming connection pushes chat messages with resume tokens instead of costly polling.

mechanisms.name: Channel predictions voting
mechanisms.why: Viewers wager points on outcomes, driving participation during a stream.

mechanisms.name: Hype train engagement meter
mechanisms.why: A shared progress meter rewards communal subscribing and cheering with escalating levels.

mechanisms.name: Webhook events and unofficial chat socket
mechanisms.why: Signed webhooks report chat and stream status while community tools read chat through a Pusher socket.

mechanisms.name: Client side multi rendition encoding
mechanisms.why: Streamers send several qualities from their GPU so viewers on weak networks still get a stream.

mechanisms.name: Drops reward campaigns
mechanisms.why: Watching time earns in game rewards linked through entitlements and fulfillment.

mechanisms.name: Interactive extensions on the video player
mechanisms.why: Panel, overlay and component extensions let viewers interact with the stream without leaving it.

mechanisms.name: WebRTC ingest with WHIP
mechanisms.why: A standard HTTP signaling step lets browsers and encoders publish live video over WebRTC.

mechanisms.name: Background audio continuity
mechanisms.why: Listening continues when the tab is hidden or the screen locks, which is the main use case.

mechanisms.name: Cross-device playback handoff (Connect)
mechanisms.why: One account can control and move playback between phone, speaker and desktop, with state mirrored on all devices.

mechanisms.name: Gapless playback and crossfade
mechanisms.why: Album and mix listening breaks if track changes add silence or volume dips.

mechanisms.name: Lock screen and media key controls
mechanisms.why: Playback must be controllable from the lock screen, headset and keyboard without opening the app.

mechanisms.name: Offline downloads of tracks and episodes
mechanisms.why: Paid tiers sell on listening without a connection, so storage and license refresh matter.

mechanisms.name: Collaborative playlists
mechanisms.why: Shared editing of a list creates social stickiness; Spotify reported 200 million listening hours on them in a month.

mechanisms.name: Selectable lossless and hi-res quality tiers
mechanisms.why: Users pick fidelity versus data use; the app must check codec and output capability.

mechanisms.name: Name your price purchase and fan collection
mechanisms.why: Direct artist sales with a public collection replace streaming royalties as the core value.

mechanisms.name: Time-synced and karaoke lyrics
mechanisms.why: Line and syllable timed lyrics turn passive listening into singing along, including offline for Spotify Premium.

mechanisms.name: Waveform with timed comments
mechanisms.why: Comments pinned to a point on the waveform make audio social and scrubbable.

mechanisms.name: Variable playback speed with pitch preservation
mechanisms.why: Heavy listeners run 1.5x to 3x, and Pocket Casts goes to 5x on web and desktop.

mechanisms.name: Reading and listening position sync across devices
mechanisms.why: Resume exactly where you left off on any device; Kindle syncs furthest page, notes and highlights.

mechanisms.name: Chapters, bookmarks and audio clips
mechanisms.why: Chapter navigation and one tap bookmarks make long audio navigable and shareable.

mechanisms.name: Background episode downloads and auto download
mechanisms.why: New episodes arrive before the commute without opening the app.

mechanisms.name: Silence trimming and volume boost
mechanisms.why: Removes pauses and levels quiet voices; Pocket Casts offers Mild, Medium and Mad Max, mobile only.

mechanisms.name: Sleep timer with end of episode option
mechanisms.why: Bedtime listening needs auto stop that does not lose the place.

mechanisms.name: Text selection highlights and shared quotes
mechanisms.why: Select a passage to highlight or quote; Medium popularized public highlights, with a toggle to hide others.

mechanisms.name: Text to speech and voiceover for articles
mechanisms.why: Turns written posts into audio; Substack adds auto voiceovers and writer recorded audio gated by paywall.

mechanisms.name: Real time AR lenses on the camera feed
mechanisms.why: Playful face and world effects are the main reason people open Snapchat's camera.

mechanisms.name: Duet and Stitch reaction recording
mechanisms.why: Turns viewers into creators by recording alongside or after another clip.

mechanisms.name: First chunk prefetch of upcoming videos
mechanisms.why: Prefetching the opening seconds hides latency but wastes data when clips are skipped.

mechanisms.name: For You feed ranked on interaction signals
mechanisms.why: The feed itself, not a follow graph, decides what each person watches.

mechanisms.name: Remix tools: green screen, cut and collab
mechanisms.why: Lets creators sample another video as background, segment or side by side layout.

mechanisms.name: Sound off by default, tap to unmute
mechanisms.why: Browsers allow muted autoplay only, so feeds start silent and unmute after a gesture.

mechanisms.name: Vertical swipe feed with adjacent video preload
mechanisms.why: The next and previous clips are ready in memory, so swipes feel instant.

mechanisms.name: Preloading paused under CPU or I/O pressure
mechanisms.why: Stops background fetching from making a busy phone stutter.

mechanisms.name: Prefetch depth tied to connection quality and data saver
mechanisms.why: Cuts waste on slow or metered links while keeping fast links smooth.

mechanisms.name: Creator controls over who can duet, stitch or remix
mechanisms.why: Gives creators consent over reuse, which keeps remix culture safe to join.

mechanisms.name: Shorts feed ranked on viewed versus swiped away
mechanisms.why: The swipe is a clean, instant feedback signal for ranking and for creators.

mechanisms.name: One player instance serving many preloaded clips
mechanisms.why: Avoids the memory and startup cost of a new player per clip.

mechanisms.name: Trial Reels shown to non-followers first
mechanisms.why: Lets creators test a clip safely before it reaches their audience.

mechanisms.name: Adaptive bitrate streaming over Media Source Extensions
mechanisms.why: Lets the player switch quality mid-playback so video starts fast and rarely stalls.

mechanisms.name: Caption and subtitle tracks with user styling
mechanisms.why: Accessibility and international reach depend on selectable, restylable text tracks.

mechanisms.name: Codec, HDR and hardware capability negotiation
mechanisms.why: Chooses 4K, HDR, Dolby or AV1 only when the device can really play them.

mechanisms.name: DRM via Encrypted Media Extensions
mechanisms.why: Studios require licensed, hardware backed decryption before premium titles will play.

mechanisms.name: Lock screen and notification media controls
mechanisms.why: Play, pause and seek from the lock screen, headphones and notification shade.

mechanisms.name: Muted autoplay previews on hover and in rows
mechanisms.why: Motion previews sell a title in seconds, and browsers allow them only when muted.

mechanisms.name: Offline downloads with expiry licenses
mechanisms.why: Lets people watch on planes and in dead zones, with rights enforced by persistent licenses.

mechanisms.name: Personalized home and up next recommendations
mechanisms.why: Ranking by watch and search history is how viewers find something to play.

mechanisms.name: Cast to a TV with Remote Playback
mechanisms.why: Moves viewing from phone to the big screen with one tap.

mechanisms.name: Skip intro and skip recap button
mechanisms.why: Removes repeated openings so binge viewing flows without scrubbing.

mechanisms.name: Automatic downloads of next episode and recommendations
mechanisms.why: Fills the phone with the right shows over Wi-Fi so offline mode is never empty.

mechanisms.name: Google Cast sender and Presentation API sessions
mechanisms.why: Drives a receiver app with queue, volume and transport control after the session starts.

mechanisms.name: Document Picture in Picture for custom player UI
mechanisms.why: Floats a whole custom player with its own controls, not just a bare video.

mechanisms.name: Live origin plus ISP embedded CDN delivery
mechanisms.why: Keeps huge live audiences from overwhelming servers, so streams hold up at peak.

mechanisms.name: Low latency live streaming with partial segments
mechanisms.why: Cuts live delay so sports and events feel near real time.

mechanisms.name: Per-title and per-shot encoding ladders
mechanisms.why: Spends bits where each title or scene needs them, so picture quality rises while data use falls.

mechanisms.name: Personalized title artwork via contextual bandits
mechanisms.why: Shows each member the thumbnail most likely to make them press play.

mechanisms.name: Picture in Picture video window
mechanisms.why: Keeps playback floating while the viewer does other things.

mechanisms.name: Watch together sessions (SharePlay, group watch)
mechanisms.why: Synchronized playback makes remote viewing social.

mechanisms.name: Hardware decoded video via WebCodecs
mechanisms.why: Gives frame level control and efficient decode for custom players and thumbnails.

mechanisms.name: X-Ray cast, music and trivia overlay on pause
mechanisms.why: Answers who is that actor or what is that song without leaving the show.
